requirement: EmDash media deletion distinguishes page references, library storage, and cached public URLs

oracle.ref: PR #1343 (fix); fix evidence: Issue #1304: origin deletion does not establish that a public URL served through an edge cache is unavailable.
oracle.invariant: The EmDash prompt says content_update removes a picture reference from a page; media_delete removes its media-library record and stored file, leaves page references unchanged, and may break them. The prompt says media_delete does not revoke a public URL and cannot promise cached URLs stop serving; it adds no purge or deny integration. When storageDeleted is true, the successful media_delete response says the stored file was deleted, page references remain, and a cached public URL may still serve; it forbids claiming the URL is revoked or unreachable. When storageDeleted is false, the response says the library record was removed but the stored file may remain and may still be served from origin; it does not claim the file is gone, and says a cached public URL may still serve. The unconfirmed media_delete asks the customer before any delete call; the confirmation gate is unchanged.
oracle.productSourcesScope: file-level: the files the case imports, reads or runs (declaration line, or the first code line); the invariant is exercised through them, the executed assertion is the case command

writes: run dir under QA_ARTIFACT_ROOT: logs/, tmp/<case> (the child TMPDIR, removed after the run)

assertionIds: the tracy_emdash description is the road (T9)
the EmDash prompt separates page removal, library deletion, and public URL revocation
a confirmed media_delete with storageDeleted:true reports file removal without claiming the public URL was revoked
a confirmed media_delete with storageDeleted:false says the stored file may remain and still serve
each of the ten destructive tools asks first, with no exec
